title: Kenyan Chapati Roll
community: Urban Kenya — the quintessential Nairobi street food
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Chapati Roll — a freshly made chapati spread with a thin egg omelette, filled with kachumbari and pili pili sauce, then rolled into a tight log and eaten on the go. The quintessential Nairobi street breakfast and lunch — fast, filling, and completely Kenyan.
longDesc: The chapati roll is one of Nairobi's most beloved street foods — a hot chapati spread with spiced egg, filled with fresh kachumbari, rolled and eaten on the way to work or school. At every school gate, bus stop, and market entrance, the chapati roll vendor is a fixture of Nairobi morning life.
steps: Beat eggs with milk, salt, and pepper.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat.
Place a chapati in the pan.
Pour half the egg mixture over the chapati. Let it spread naturally.
Allow the egg to set partially — 1—2 minutes.
Flip the chapati-egg together. Cook for 30 seconds.
Remove from heat. Add kachumbari and pili pili along one edge.
Roll firmly into a tight log.
Wrap in paper for street food style or serve on a plate.
chefTips: The egg should be just set — not dry — when you roll.
Roll immediately while hot and flexible.
Street style: wrap tightly in newsprint or paper for structural support.
commonMistakes: Overcooked egg — dry and cracks when rolling.
Waiting too long to roll — the chapati stiffens.
cookingScience: Pouring the egg directly onto the chapati in the pan creates a bonded egg-chapati layer — the egg adheres to the chapati surface as it sets, creating a unified sheet that rolls without separating.
sustainabilityTips: Eggs and chapati are among the most affordable, sustainable protein-and-carbohydrate combinations in Kenya.
culturalNote: The chapati roll is Nairobi's most beloved on-the-go breakfast — the snack that fuels the city's early mornings. Every school child knows it; every office worker has eaten it standing at a street stall before catching a matatu.
